answer_1.quote: Sentence simplification is the task of rewriting text to make it easier to read, while preserving its main meaning and important information ... We evaluate our approach on the Newsela and WikiLarge corpora.

answer_2.quote: We use the SARI metric to measure the simplicity of the generated sentences. ... We also compute the BLEU score to measure the closeness between a candidate and a reference. ... We also include a few intrinsic measures ... the Flesch‑Kincaid grade level (FKGL) evaluating the ease of reading, as well as the average length of the sentence.

answer_4.quote: We conducted a human evaluation on the Newsela dataset ... measure the adequacy (How much meaning from the original sentence is preserved?), simplicity (Is the output simpler than the original sentence?), and fluency (Is the output grammatical?) on a five‑point Likert scale. ... we also asked the volunteers to measure the number of instances where models produce incorrect details or generate text that is not implied by the original sentence.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators (three volunteers) rated each output on adequacy, simplicity, fluency using a 1‑5 Likert scale and counted false information per sentence.
